messages.subject: BUGS code for Chandler & Royle (2013)
parts:
Has anyone written any BUGS code to implement  the models in Chandler & Royle (2013). "Spatially explicit models for inference about density in unmarked or partially marked populations". The Annals of Applied Statistics 7:936-954?

I have code working for the aggregated count version of the model (below), but I'm having trouble figuring out how to write the version which includes the latent encounter data z[i,j,k] | w[i]. This is necessary to incorporate information on individual identities.

Thanks,
Eric

 model {

    # priors
    sigma ~ dnorm(250,1/50)I(0,)
    lambda.0 ~ dbeta(1,1)
    psi ~ dbeta(1,1)
 
    for(i in 1:M) {
    w[i] ~ dbern(psi)
    S[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1],xlim[2])
    S[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1],ylim[2])
    
    for(j in 1:J) {
    d2[i,j]<- (S[i,1] - X[j,1])^2 + (S[i,2] - X[j,2])^2
    lambda.ij[i,j]<- exp(-d2[i,j]/(2*sigma^2))*w[i]    

    }
    }
    
    for(j in 1:J) {
    lambda.j[j]<- lambda.0*sum(lambda.ij[,j])
    n[j] ~ dpois(K*lambda.j[j])  
    }
    
    N<- sum(w)
    }

messages.subject: Re: BUGS code for Chandler & Royle (2013)
parts:
To follow-up on my question, I received 2 answers that pointed to published versions of the BUGS model.


Dana Morin wrote:

Hi Eric,

 I used it for a mark-resight model with lions a couple years ago (Kane et al. 2015). I've attached the paper and the supplementary appendix with the code (show the code for both marked and unmarked components). Hope that helps!

Best,

Dana


The paper is:

Kane, M. D., D. J. Morin, and M. J. Kelly. 2015. Potential for camera-traps and spatial mark-resight models to improve monitoring of the critically endangered West African lion (Panthera leo). Biodiversity and Conservation 24:3527-3541.

https://doi.org/10.1007/s10531-015-1012-7

 

Richard Chandler wrote:

Hi Eric,

There is some code in chapter 18 of our book, but that code uses dsum instead of the new and improved sum distribution in JAGS. Try something like this:

model {

    # priors

    sigma ~ dnorm(250,1/50)I(0,)

    lambda.0 ~ dbeta(1,1)

    psi ~ dbeta(1,1)

 

    for(i in 1:M) {

    w[i] ~ dbern(psi)

    S[i,1] ~ dunif(xlim[1],xlim[2])

    S[i,2] ~ dunif(ylim[1],ylim[2])

 

    for(j in 1:J) {

    d2[i,j]<- (S[i,1] - X[j,1])^2 + (S[i,2] - X[j,2])^2

lambda[i,j]<- exp(-d2[i,j]/(2*sigma^2))*w[i]   

    y[i,j] ~ dpois(lambda[i,j])

    }

    }

 

    for(j in 1:J) {

      n[j] ~ sum(y[,j]) 

    }

 

    N<- sum(w)

  }

Also, unless the marked individuals are a random sample of the total population, you might need to model the marking process. There are a couple of recent spatial mark-resight papers about this issue.

Richard
